title: SQL
examples: How do I select specific columns from a table?
What is the difference between WHERE and JOIN?
Can I sort the results after I query the data?

explain.say: Today we are learning how to ask questions of databases using SQL.
The SELECT statement tells the database which columns you want to see.
The WHERE clause lets you filter records based on specific conditions.

items: Step 1: Start with the table name
Step 2: Use WHERE to set a condition
Step 3: The database returns matching rows

explain.say: The ORDER BY clause lets you sort the final results by a specific column.

items: Ascending: A to Z or 1 to 10
Descending: Z to A or 10 to 1

draw.text: SELECT FROM table ORDER BY column DESC

explain.say: To combine data from two tables, you use the JOIN keyword.

draw.text: SELECT FROM TableA JOIN TableB ON key

explain.say: Imagine you want to see student names and the class they are in.

draw.text: SELECT name, classname FROM Students JOIN Classes ON studentid = classid

faq.q: What is the difference between SELECT and FROM?
faq.a: SELECT specifies the columns you want to retrieve. FROM specifies the table that holds those columns.
asks: Do I need both SELECT and FROM?

faq.q: When should I use the WHERE clause?
faq.a: Use WHERE when you only want to see data that meets certain criteria, like only records from last year.
asks: How do I filter my results?
Can I put conditions in the SELECT statement?

faq.q: What does JOIN do in SQL?
faq.a: JOIN combines rows from two or more tables based on a related column they share.
asks: How do I link two tables together?

faq.q: Can I sort by multiple columns?
faq.a: Yes, you can list multiple columns in the ORDER BY clause, separated by commas.
asks: How do I sort by name then by age?
Does ORDER BY only work on one column?

faq.q: Do I need to use JOIN every time I write a query?
faq.a: No, you only need JOIN when the data you want is spread across multiple related tables.
asks: What if the data is all in one table?

facts: The SELECT statement specifies the columns you want to retrieve.
The WHERE clause filters records based on specified conditions.
The JOIN clause combines records from two or more tables.
ORDER BY sorts the final result set by one or more columns.

quiz.say: To find all student records where the grade is greater than 70, which clause do you use?
quiz.why: The WHERE clause is specifically designed to filter rows based on conditions like grade greater than 70.

wrong.0: SELECT tells you what columns to show, not which rows to keep.
wrong.1: JOIN is used to combine data from different tables, not to filter one table.
wrong.2: ORDER BY only changes the sequence of the results, it does not filter them.

quiz.say: If you want to see the names and scores, and sort them by score from highest to lowest, what is the correct structure?
quiz.show: SELECT name, score FROM Scores ORDER BY score DESC
quiz.why: You must use ORDER BY and specify DESC to sort the results from highest to lowest.

wrong.0: Using WHERE here would only filter records, it would not change the sorting order.
wrong.1: DESC is a modifier for ORDER BY, not for the SELECT statement itself.
wrong.2: JOIN is for linking tables, it has nothing to do with sorting the results.

quiz.say: To get the name from the Students table and the major from the Majors table, using the studentmajorid key, what do you write?
quiz.show: SELECT S.name, M.major FROM Students S JOIN Majors M ON S.studentmajorid = M.majorid
quiz.why: You need JOIN to connect the two tables, and ON specifies the matching key between them.

wrong.0: ORDER BY is for sorting the final output, not for combining the initial data sets.
wrong.2: Using WHERE here would only filter records, it would not combine the data from both tables.
wrong.3: You must specify the join condition using ON to tell the database how the tables relate.
